chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, who said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad and others narrated to me, linking it up through their chain to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him),

that he said: A believer is one whose earnings are pure, whose character is good, whose inner self is sound, who spends the surplus of his wealth, restrains the surplus of his speech, and whom people are secure from his evil, and who treats people fairly with regard to himself.
ai.seo_question: What are the defining characteristics of a believer according to Imam Ali (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith as a comprehensive ethical framework where internal sincerity (seriyyah) manifests in external social conduct. It underscores the Shia emphasis on the integration of spiritual purity with tangible social justice, particularly through financial generosity and self-accountability (ansaf al-nas min nafs). This narrative serves as a practical guide for the believer's daily interactions, reflecting the holistic nature of faith in Twelver Shi'ism.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 7-31 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted Muhammad ibn Yahya, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad and others who linked it up through a chain of narrators to the Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali (MGB), “

A believer is one whose business is legitimate; is good-tempered; has a good soul; gives charity from his excessive wealth; doesn’t talk a lot; the people are secure with him; and he treats others fairly.”
